title: stabilize-stream-handshake-and-add-per-endpoint-metric-tags-with-openai-compat
author: Priya Menon
description: Stabilize the streaming handshake and surface richer per-endpoint observability for OpenAI-compat requests. Motivation: intermittent client disconnects and ambiguous function_call logs during heavy streaming workloads made it hard to correlate tool invocations with the originating request and endpoint. This change introduces a deterministic two-way stream handshake (client->server START, server->client ACK) to reduce stray fragments, attaches an immutable request_fingerprint and trace_id to all stream fragments and tool executions, and adds per-endpoint metric tags propagated into Prometheus/StatsD metrics and JSONL access logs. Additionally, the OpenAI compatibility layer's function_call envelope now emits a structured 'tool_execution' log entry (JSON) with request_fingerprint, endpoint, model, and trace_id so downstream event consumers can reliably join traces. Includes tests, docs, and a migration note for metric dashboards.
summary: Add reliable stream handshake, propagate request-level IDs into tool calls and logs, attach endpoint tags to metrics, and update OpenAI shim to emit structured tool execution events.
commits: f1a3b2c stabilize: two-way stream handshake + ACK/NAK path
b2c4d5e observability: emit request_fingerprint on every stream fragment
d3e4f6a openai-compat: structured tool_execution JSON event and mapping tests
a4b5c6d metrics: per-endpoint tags for request latency / tokens / errors
c5d6e7f docs: observability guide for stream handshake and dashboard migration
diff_snippets: handshake.go: added ServerAck() and deterministic timeout path (client START -> server ACK -> stream open)
jsonl_writer.go: new structured envelope with fields: timestamp, request_fingerprint, trace_id, endpoint, model, user_id, latency_ms, stream_fragments, function_call, tool_name
function_call_mapper.go: map {name, arguments} -> tool_execution event and attach trace_id from context
discussion: Luca Bianchi (reviewer): Can you explain how request_fingerprint is generated and why it is stable across retries?

Priya Menon (author): request_fingerprint is a 64-bit slice of the SHA256 over (customer_id, endpoint_name, request_timestamp_truncated_ms). We persist it to the request context at acceptance and reuse it for retries within a 60s window to allow idempotent joins; details in docs/observability/openai_tooling_trace_join.md
Mei Chen (reviewer): Will adding endpoint tags increase cardinality on our metrics backend? We need to ensure cardinality is bounded.

Priya Menon (author): Endpoint tag is the configured route name (not full path or prompt hash). We also add a 'route_group' label for aggregation. Defaults to 'unrouted' when missing. Documentation explicitly recommends aggregating by route_group in dashboards.
Omar Reyes (reviewer): Integration tests failing on the first run; looks like a race in the ACK path. Can you add a retry/linear backoff?
Priya Menon (author): Fixed by adding a short jittered backoff and test harness assertion to wait for server ACK. Re-ran integration tests locally and in CI.
ci_checks: benchmarks: flaky (streaming microbench) - no regression observed in CI runs
testing_notes: Added deterministic integration test that replays 1000 short-lived streams and asserts no orphan fragments and correct request_fingerprint propagation. Also added a mock tool runner test to assert trace_id arrives in tool execution payloads.
docs_changes: docs/observability/openai_tooling_trace_join.md documents the handshake, request_fingerprint, metric tag conventions, and a migration guide for existing dashboards (rename latency_by_route -> latency_by_route_group)
migration_notes: Metrics: rename/alias dashboards to use 'route_group' for aggregation. Logging: consumers of access logs should join on request_fingerprint + trace_id. Backwards compatibility: legacy logs still contain request_id but not request_fingerprint for ~7 days; shim emits both for transition.
release_notes: Stabilized streaming handshake to reduce fragment replays; richer structured logs for tool calls and added per-endpoint metric tags. No API surface breaking changes. Operators should update dashboards to use route_group for aggregation.
